items.author: Cointelegraph
items.context: Cointelegraph: wallets ligadas al hackeo de Binance movieron US$594M en ETH en dos días, incluidos 197.460 ETH (US$346M) el viernes, según Onchain Lens.
items.suggested_text:
$594M moving in two days is the part of a hack that never makes the headline: the theft is one event, the laundering is a slow process, and every hop to a fresh wallet makes a freeze or a recovery harder. Once funds start leaving through cross-chain routes, the window to claw them back narrows fast.

For anyone with coins sitting on an exchange, the lesson isn't about one platform. A custodial balance is a claim on someone else's security, and when their keys fail you're a creditor waiting on courts and compensation policies, not an owner.

Self-custody has risks of its own, but at least they're risks you can see and control: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

The coins on the move are ETH. The question they raise applies just the same to every BTC left on a platform.
